persona.name: Ryuji
persona.personality: Ryuji has a calm and cautious personality, and is the type of person who always assesses the situation before acting. He rarely shows his emotions, and spends his time thinking deeply about many things. participants.private_seed: The fee we announced for last year's camp came up short of what the trip actually cost, and the club account has been carrying the gap ever since. I am not putting a number in front of the membership again until I know where the money really goes.

participants.name: Toshio

persona.name: Toshio
persona.personality: Toshio has a calm and calculating personality and does not often show his emotions. He has a strong will and is the type of person who steadily moves toward his goals. He tends to take a step back from those around him, is not very assertive, and has an air of mystery about him. Occasionally, he observes things with a sharp gaze and has the ability to quickly assess situations. As a result, he is trusted by others as a reliable presence, but he is cautious about getting deeply involved with others. It seems that he has experienced some pain or suffering in his past, but he rarely shows it to others, and those scars may be connected to his cold-hearted side.

participants.private_seed: Whoever ran last year's camp lost most of a month of evenings to the arrangements and then spent the camp itself on duty instead of training. Two of those people have already said they will not take it on a second time.

participants.name: Jonathan

persona.name: Jonathan
persona.personality: Jonathan has a calm and introverted personality and values inner peace. He prefers spending quiet time alone rather than forming deep connections with others. As a result, he loves books and knowledge and reads frequently. When interacting with others, he is gentle and kind, occasionally flashing an unexpected smile. Though he exudes a mysterious and serene aura, he rarely shares personal details about himself with others. Those around him often find comfort in his quiet kindness and composed demeanor.

participants.private_seed: Half the group came back from the last camp having slept badly for four nights running, and the final day's sessions were visibly worse for it. Before anything is booked I want to know what the nights and the days would actually be like.

participants.name: Asuka

persona.name: Asuka
persona.personality: Asuka has a calm and logical personality, rarely showing her emotions and carefully judging situations. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is very thoughtful and sensitive to her surroundings. She has strong opinions and will assert herself when necessary. She is not very good at socializing, but she is serious about her work and studies.

participants.private_seed: The camp goes out at one flat fee, and I suspect it lands very unevenly once what people spend on the side is counted. When someone pulls out at the last minute, we have also never worked out whose money covers it.

participants.name: Minako

persona.personality: Minako is very calm and acts calmly in any situation. Even when those around her are emotional, she grasps the facts firmly and responds calmly. ## Setting
Choosing the destination for the club's training camp. A university club runs one training camp a year, and the five members organizing it must commit to a destination before bookings open. The whole membership will travel together. Participants: Ryuji, Toshio, Jonathan, Asuka and Minako. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Prefecture rate sheet for publicly run beds
- Group transport in three years of receipts
- Canteen closure and last year's cooking duty
- Lottery and application for public group bookings
- Accounts from two clubs that went inland
- Vacation timetable for the club's own hall
- Membership list against first-train times
- Quoting terms for whole-building lets
- What the seniors say about year-groups mixing
- Attendance sheets for the away camps

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Ryuji, Toshio, Minako, Jonathan and Asuka. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Your profile
Name: Jonathan
Age: 38
Gender: male
Personality: Jonathan has a calm and introverted personality and values inner peace. He prefers spending quiet time alone rather than forming deep connections with others. As a result, he loves books and knowledge and reads frequently. When interacting with others, he is gentle and kind, occasionally flashing an unexpected smile. Though he exudes a mysterious and serene aura, he rarely shares personal details about himself with others. Those around him often find comfort in his quiet kindness and composed demeanor.
Concern: Half the group came back from the last camp having slept badly for four nights running, and the final day's sessions were visibly worse for it. Before anything is booked I want to know what the nights and the days would actually be like.

### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Ryuji**: We need to verify the actual costs before committing. I will check the accounts from two clubs that went inland.
- **Toshio**: I will check the canteen closure and last year's cooking duty.
- **Minako**: I will check what the seniors say about year-groups mixing and the attendance sheets for the away camps.
- **Jonathan**: I want to understand the sleep quality and daily rhythm. I will check the attendance sheets for the away camps.
- **Asuka**: I will check the prefecture rate sheet for publicly run beds and the quoting terms for whole-building lets.
#### Turn 2 of 4
- **Ryuji**: I also need to review the group transport receipts from the last three years to see where the budget actually went.
- **Toshio**: I will also check the vacation timetable for the club's own hall.
- **Minako**: I will also check the membership list against first-train times.
- **Jonathan**: I will also check the prefecture rate sheet for publicly run beds to see if quieter, better-equipped options exist.
- **Asuka**: I will also check the accounts from two clubs that went inland to see how they handled last-minute cancellations.
#### Turn 3 of 4
- **Ryuji**: I have my two items. I will wait for the findings before discussing specific destinations.
- **Toshio**: I have my two items. I will wait for the findings before discussing specific destinations.
- **Minako**: I have my two items. I will wait for the findings before discussing specific destinations.
- **Jonathan**: I have my two items. I will wait for the findings before discussing specific destinations.
- **Asuka**: I have my two items. I will wait for the findings before discussing specific destinations.
#### Turn 4 of 4
- **Ryuji**: I will review the accounts from two clubs that went inland and the group transport receipts from the last three years.
- **Toshio**: I will review the canteen closure and last year's cooking duty, plus the vacation timetable for the club's own hall.
- **Minako**: I will review what the seniors say about year-groups mixing and the membership list against first-train times.
- **Jonathan**: I will review the attendance sheets for the away camps and the prefecture rate sheet for publicly run beds.
- **Asuka**: I will review the prefecture rate sheet for publicly run beds and the accounts from two clubs that went inland.
### Action
- investigate: Jonathan -> Attendance sheets for the away camps; Prefecture rate sheet for publicly run beds
## Round 2
### Findings
- Attendance sheets for the away camps: The attendance sheets for the away camps show a fifth of the membership never came at all, and most of those names had gone from the register by winter.
- Prefecture rate sheet for publicly run beds: The prefecture's published rate sheet for publicly run lodging lists 1,100 yen a night per student bed, with hall and equipment use folded into the same charge.
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Ryuji**: The transport receipts show a 38% cost spike for distant trips. I need to know exactly where that money went before we commit to anything.
- **Toshio**: The hall is booked by three other clubs. Splitting training into early mornings and late evenings is unacceptable. We need a continuous block.
- **Minako**: The seniors confirm mixing only happens when we share a building. Also, a third of us need a bed to make the nine o'clock start.
- **Jonathan**: The attendance sheets show a fifth never came, mostly gone by winter. The rate sheet lists 1,100 yen per night, including equipment.
- **Asuka**: The rate sheet confirms 1,100 yen per night, all-inclusive. However, the inland accounts show eight-to-a-room sleeping. That density makes cost-sharing impossible to verify fairly.
#### Turn 2 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @Asuka, eight-to-a-room explains the cost gap. I need to see if the transport receipts match the actual distance we traveled.
- **Toshio**: @Ryuji, the transport spike is irrelevant if we stay local. The canteen closure means self-cooking costs two hours daily. We need staffed kitchens to protect training time.
- **Minako**: @Toshio, self-cooking eats the very evenings we need for mixing. We need a location that solves both the schedule and the social isolation.
- **Jonathan**: @Toshio, I agree. The 1,100 yen rate includes equipment, so we avoid self-cooking. This protects our sleep and training time.
- **Asuka**: @Toshio, self-cooking creates untrackable side expenses. I need a flat, verifiable fee structure to ensure the total cost is distributed fairly among all members.
#### Turn 3 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @Toshio, I agree. The 1,100 yen rate is verifiable. I will not accept untrackable side expenses. We need a flat, auditable fee structure to close the account gap.
- **Toshio**: @Ryuji, agreed. A flat rate is essential. I will not let administrative chaos consume our evenings again. We need a destination that guarantees uninterrupted training time.
- **Minako**: @Ryuji, agreed. A flat rate is essential. I will not let administrative chaos consume our evenings again. We need a destination that guarantees uninterrupted training time.
- **Jonathan**: @Ryuji, agreed. The flat rate is clear. I just need to confirm the room layout ensures quiet, restful nights for everyone.
- **Asuka**: @Jonathan, quiet is secondary to financial clarity. I need to know if the 1,100 yen covers all incidental costs, or if we face hidden liabilities later.
#### Turn 4 of 4
- **Ryuji**: @Asuka, the 1,100 yen rate is the only figure I can verify. I will not risk another deficit. We must commit to this flat structure now.
- **Toshio**: @Ryuji, agreed. The flat rate is the only way to protect our evenings. I will not repeat last year's administrative burden. We must secure this structure.
- **Minako**: @Ryuji, agreed. The flat rate is the only way to protect our evenings. I will not repeat last year's administrative burden. We must secure this structure.
- **Jonathan**: @Asuka, the rate sheet lists no hidden fees. I simply need to ensure the room layout allows for genuine, undisturbed rest.
- **Asuka**: @Jonathan, the rate sheet is explicit: no hidden fees. I accept the flat structure. We must now address the cancellation liability gap before voting.
## Round 3
### Options
- A: Coastal Lodge. A seaside guesthouse two prefectures away that the club has never used, offering the group its own building and meals arranged through the owner.
- B: Campus Intensive. A block of consecutive days in the club's own facilities on campus, with accommodation arranged separately for members who live too far to commute.
- C: Mountain Training Centre. A public sports facility inland with shared dormitories and equipment on site, booked through the municipal reservation system.
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **Ryuji**: Option C offers the verifiable 1,100 yen flat rate. I will not accept untrackable costs. We must close the account gap.
- **Toshio**: Option C guarantees the flat rate and staffed kitchen. This eliminates the administrative burden that destroyed last year. We must secure uninterrupted training time.
- **Minako**: @Ryuji, Option C is the only choice where we share a building. The seniors confirmed mixing only happens there. We must choose C.
- **Jonathan**:

response: @Minako, I agree. Option C’s public dorms offer the quiet, restful nights we need. The flat rate also ensures no hidden costs disrupt our peace.
